Dissertation
Opacity and Adaptation under Sanctions. Geoeconomics in the Universe of Russian Firms. Claremont Graduate University, expected 2026.

Sanctions can disrupt firms' access to markets and finance while increasing the value of withholding financial information. The dissertation follows the financial statements of the universe of Russian firms to see which firms stay visible and how they adjusted.

Chapter 2 · Opacity Chapter 3 · Adaptation Methods and data

Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Did firms' financial statements leave public view?

In 2021, the last financial year before the invasion, 63.4% of eligible firms had a statement in the public archive.

Public statements did not become scarcer after 2022.

You drew for 2024. The share was 66.3%. You expected a fall, and the share rose.You expected little change, and the share rose.You expected a rise, and the share rose. Your line ended within two points of the data.

Among all eligible firms the share with an available statement rose from 63.4% in 2021 to 66.3% in 2024.

Among firms registered at year-end it was 71.7% in 2021 and 71.2% in 2024. The rise in the first share comes from the firms counted.

The number of statements fell by 2.0%, from 2,129,509 to 2,086,055, while the eligible population fell by 6.2%, from 3,357,109 to 3,147,504. The share rose as firms without statements left the register.

Rosstat supplied the statements for the years through 2018 and the Federal Tax Service (FNS) those from 2019, so the two periods are read separately.

Years

The archive holds about as many statements for 2024 as for 2021. Both years come from one release, so this comparison cannot count restrictions that removed earlier statements as well as later ones. Chapter 2 shows which firms stay visible and where the others went.
